fba.title: Functional Behavior Assessment (FBA)
fba.description: Identifies the function of challenging behaviors to design evidence-based interventions (Malott, Ch. 18-22)

sections.title: 🎯 Target Behavior Identification
sections.description: Define the behavior operationally (observable and measurable)

questions.label: Operational description of the behavior
questions.placeholder: Describe exactly what the child does: specific movements, vocalizations, approximate duration. E.g.: "Throws themselves on the floor, kicks with both legs and screams loudly for 2-10 minutes"
questions.helpText: A good operational definition describes TOPOGRAPHY (how it looks), not intentions

questions.label: How often does the behavior occur?
Are there other behaviors that occur together with this one?
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Before throwing objects, they clench their fists and grind their teeth...

questions.label: Does it pose a risk of physical harm?

sections.title: 🌡️ Antecedents (A of the ABC)
sections.description: What happens BEFORE the behavior? Context, triggers, conditions

questions.label: In what contexts/environments does it occur most?
In what contexts does it almost NEVER occur?
What are the most common triggers?
Motivating operations: what conditions increase the likelihood?
Is there a specific Sd (discriminative stimulus) that almost always precedes the behavior?
questions.placeholder: E.g.: When the therapist takes out the workbook, when they say "it is time to..."

questions.label: How much time passes between the trigger and the behavior?

sections.title: ⚡ Consequences (C of the ABC)
sections.description: What happens AFTER the behavior? What maintains it?

questions.label: What happens after the behavior?
options: Obtains a desired object or activity

questions.label: Who usually responds to the behavior?
Are the consequences consistent across caregivers?
options: Partially - some do, others do not

questions.label: Does the behavior achieve what it seems to seek?

sections.title: 🧪 Functional Hypothesis
sections.description: Based on A-B-C, what is the maintaining function of the behavior?

questions.label: Primary function hypothesis
options: Automatic reinforcement - Reduction of internal discomfort

questions.label: Evidence supporting this hypothesis
questions.placeholder: Describe the observed patterns that lead to this functional conclusion...

questions.label: Complete functional statement
questions.placeholder: In the presence of [Antecedent], [Name] exhibits [Behavior], and as a result obtains/escapes [Consequence], which increases the future likelihood of the behavior.

questions.label: Is there an alternative behavior that fulfills the same function appropriately?
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Can ask for help verbally, can use a "break" card, can point to what they want...

questions.label: What skills do they need to develop to use the alternative behavior?
Evaluator's additional observations
questions.placeholder: Additional patterns, important contextual factors, overall clinical impression...

bip.title: Behavior Intervention Plan (BIP)
bip.description: Structured intervention plan for challenging behaviors, based on the function identified in the FBA

questions.label: Target behavior (operational definition)
questions.placeholder: Copy or summarize the operational definition from the FBA

questions.label: Reduction goal
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Reduce tantrum behavior from a frequency of 5/day to 1/day over an 8-week period, with a 1-month maintenance criterion

sections.title: 🛡️ Antecedent Strategies (Prevention)
sections.description: Modifications to the environment BEFORE the behavior occurs

questions.label: What changes to the physical environment will be implemented?
Will advance notice be given before transitions?
Will the difficulty of demands be adjusted?
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Start with high-probability tasks before difficult tasks (high-p sequence)

questions.label: Strategies for motivating operations
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Ensure prior rest, offer a snack before demanding sessions, allow free access to the reinforcer before work...

sections.title: 🗣️ Replacement Strategies (Teaching)
sections.description: Teach an alternative behavior that fulfills the same function

questions.label: Replacement behavior to teach
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Teach them to ask for a "break" with a PECS card or word, so it has the same escape function as the tantrum

questions.label: Method for teaching the replacement behavior
What reinforcer will be used for the replacement behavior?
questions.placeholder: The SAME reinforcer that maintains the problem behavior must be accessible via the appropriate behavior

sections.title: 📉 Consequence Strategies for the Problem Behavior
sections.description: What to do AFTER the behavior occurs (based on extinction + DRA/DRO)

questions.label: Extinction procedure
questions.placeholder: Based on the function: if escape → do not remove the demand, if attention → withdraw attention, if tangible → do not give the object...

questions.label: Will DRA, DRO or DRI be used?
options: DRA - Differential reinforcement of alternative behavior
DRO - Reinforcement of the absence of behavior

questions.label: If there is a risk of harm, how is it handled?
questions.placeholder: Safety protocol: who intervenes, how, when the session is stopped...

questions.label: Is there a documented crisis plan?
BIP success criterion
questions.placeholder: E.g.: Reduce from 5 tantrums/day to 1 or fewer/day over 3 consecutive weeks, with 4 weeks of maintenance

questions.label: How often will the plan be reviewed?
Is training for parents/teachers required?
options: No - they already know the plan
